title: Hosted API warm-start spikes causing 5xx wave during large-customer migration
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description: Summary: During a scheduled migration of a large enterprise customer onto a new dedicated-to-hosted routing path we observed a sustained spike of P95/P99 latencies and a correlated increase in 502/504/500 responses from the Hosted API. The failure mode was not a single infrastructure outage but a coordinated surge of model process warm-starts and JIT kernel compilation on a subset of GPU pools which amplified upstream proxy timeouts and client retries, resulting in a customer-visible 5xx wave. This ticket coordinates diagnosis, a short-term mitigation, and a production-grade fix to avoid recurrence.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 2026-03-01 02:14 UTC migration started; 02:20 UTC metrics show P99 CPU/GPU compile spikes; 02:25 UTC proxy queue growth -> 502s. Findings: 1) Migration traffic generated many concurrent initial requests that forced the runtime to spin up model worker processes and perform kernel selection/compilation for several large-VOC models. 2) Kernel compilation and initial KV cache population are blocking on a single worker thread per GPU causing head-of-line delays. 3) Edge proxy has a 5s upstream timeout; increased client retries produced retry amplification. 4) Some pools had older quantized binaries causing longer per-warmup compile steps. Correlation: spikes match migration time window and only affected pools in region-3, hosted-4 cluster. Evidence: flame graphs, GPU kernel compile logs, dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/hosted/warmstart/2026-03-01
fix_plan: Short-term mitigation: 1) Deploy admission holdback to limit concurrent warm-starts to 2 per pool (hotpatch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821). 2) Increase proxy upstream timeout from 5s to 12s for the affected canary region while mitigation is in flight (edge rollout PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/267). 3) Apply emergency backoff guidance to SDKs (client advisory). Long-term fix: 1) Implement asynchronous warm-start queue and cooperative JIT compilation so worker threads return quickly and compilation proceeds off the request path (design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/Async+Warm+Start+Design). 2) Precompile/ship model kernel cache during image build for frequently deployed large models. 3) Introduce a warm-start budget per tenant and better migration ramp metrics. Implementation PR tracked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4905
rollout_plan: Canary: region-3 small percentage (5%) with admission holdback and extended upstream timeout for 2h monitoring. If stable, ramp to 25% after 30m, 50% after 1h, full after 2h. Metrics to watch: P50/P95/P99 latency, 5xx rate, warm-start compile time distribution, queue length. Escalation gates: if 5xx rate > 0.25% or P99 increase > 30% over baseline revert holdback and re-evaluate. Rollback: revert PR 4821 and edge-proxy timeout change.
customer_comms: Initial customer update (03-01 03:10 UTC): briefed customer on observed 5xx surge during migration and immediate mitigation steps (admission holdback). Committed to timeline: short-term mitigation in 1 hour, stabilization monitoring for 48 hours, and a permanent fix roadmap with expected ETA 3 weeks. Customer asked for an opt-out to pause migration; accepted and paused additional migration waves until holdback verified. Sent follow-up with troubleshooting artifacts and dashboard link.
postmortem_action_items: Add precompile step for large models in CI images
Add warm-start budget and migration safety gates to console
Improve per-pool kernel-compile telemetry and alerts
Update client SDK docs with retry guidance for long warmups
notes: Follow-up: schedule a cross-team postmortem with product, infra, and solutions engineering. Check Dedicated migration playbook to add warm-start quota checks before migrations. Consider adding a console flag to pre-warm model kernels for opt-in customers. Update runbook with the admission holdback rollback command and query for compile histogram.
recent_updates: 2026-03-02: holdback PR merged and canary deployed to region-3; observed 60% reduction in 5xx. 2026-03-04: started async warm-start spike prototype; initial benchmarks show 40% reduction in head latency. 2026-03-05: customer confirmed migration resumed with no new 5xx events.
